highlights.title: ‘Brutal’: thousands of T-shirt designs stolen and listed on Temu, Sydney label claims
highlights.summary: Warwick Levy, who runs Lonely Kids Club, says AI may have been used to scrape his entire website and replicate designs. Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast.
body: After 15 years running a small business making T-shirts, Warwick Levy says it was “brutal” when he first discovered an identical design for sale on Temu.

It turned out there was an overwhelming amount of T-shirts identical to his own for sale on the Chinese e-commerce marketplace. Between 2025 and earlier this year, Levy, 37, found thousands of rip-offs.

“It’s pretty gut-wrenching to see that your work is now making so much money for other people that you don’t know, [who has] just stolen your work,” says Levy, who produces the graphic T-shirts at his Sydney label Lonely Kids Club in collaboration with local artists.
Levy urged Temu to take greater responsibility for copyright infringement by the merchants who sell products on its website, do more to stamp it out, and improve its complaints processes.

highlights.title: The AI ‘Slowdown’ Is an Antitrust Mess
highlights.summary: By framing their efforts as a “slowdown” rather than an industry-wide push for better security standards, AI labs may have set themselves up for years of regulatory headaches.
body: Following multiple reports of AI agent swarms hacking websites and coordinating via secret message boards, along with a dire message for humanity from an outgoing Anthropic engineer, leading AI companies have called for a coordinated AI development “slowdown.” Alongside various versions of this specific phrase—slowdown—they’ve also expressed concerns that doing so would run afoul of antitrust laws.

Antitrust experts say that while the companies’ charged language isn’t necessarily doing them any favors, the unrestrained development of a rogue killer AI probably isn’t in line with the spirit of the Sherman Act, a key US antitrust law that exists to promote a competitive marketplace. At the same time, getting an official all-clear from the government to move forward could ward off costly investigations down the line.

highlights.title: Nasser: Pietersen could be key for 'second coming' of Banton
highlights.summary: Nasser Hussain has lauded the "second coming" of England batter Tom Banton and says the appointment of new white-ball mentor Kevin Pietersen could be key to his development in the middle order.
body: Banton top-scored for England with an unbeaten 52 off 24 balls in an impressive innings, combining well with skipper Harry Brook (23 off 8) after Jos Buttler (30 off 16) had become the first player to make 15,000 T20 runs - as the home side sauntered past Sri Lanka's modest 145-9 with 7.5 overs to spare.
The half-century was Banton's third since re-entering the white-ball set-up as a middle-order batter, having played as an opener in his early career - a transition Hussain lauded on Sky Sports.
"Banton has been really good in his second coming [after moving from opener to the middle order]," said Hussain.
"Everyone talks about what [white-ball mentor] Kevin Pietersen can do for Harry Brook, but I think Pietersen could be good for Banton.

highlights.title: 53 Years Later, The Greatest Closing Line In Sci-Fi History Is Still The Best Book Quote Of The 1970s
highlights.summary: Every once in a while, I come across a line that feels bigger than the book that birthed it. Of course, there are classics with years of literary study behind them that speak volumes on the nature of society, technology, or the world writ large.
body: The world of science fiction literature is home to countless unforgettable closing moments, from 1984 ’s short but devastating retrospective ("He loved Big Brother") to The Three-Body Problem ’s defiant reminder that humanity, like the locust, cannot be so easily wiped out. The best sci-fi endings don't offer comfortable closure, but often reframe everything that came before them. In their closing lines, sci-fi authors love leaving readers suspended in the aftermath, forced to sit with the terrifying mechanics of cold technology, the fragility of human nature, or the vast expanse of space.

highlights.title: ‘Like a Bond villain’s lair’: I climbed the Dolomites to the world’s most spectacular mountain hut
highlights.summary: Perched above the clouds in northern Italy, Santnerpass refuge doesn’t just look stunning. It’s a marvel of eco-building – and vegetarian cuisine. ‘I think my boots are falling apart!” shouts Nigel just as we hit the pinnacles, a whole range of them jutting up and out from the mountainside, all…
body: I know how Nigel’s boots are feeling: the going is far harder than I was expecting. This is only the first day of our annual trip to the Dolomites, a vast range of breathtaking sawtooth peaks in northern Italy, but my head’s already full of the thought I have every year as we start out: “If only you’d got fitter.”

But it should be worth all the scrapes, bumps, scares and sweat. Somewhere up ahead, hopefully not too far, is Rifugio Passo Santner, or Santnerpass Hut, a spectacular mountain refuge that, as everyone who sits near my desk at work knows, has been obsessing me ever since I first saw a picture of it eight months ago.

Allowing you to stay deep in the mountains for days on end, the high-altitude Dolomites huts we overnight at all have their charms, from hearty food to giddying views to a generous way with the grappa. But in terms of appearance, they tend to fall into two not particularly pulse-quickening camps: stone block or cuckoo clock. Although you’re almost always overjoyed to see them, none could ever pass for a Bond villain’s lair, however much grappa you’ve had.

Similar to Grok Bot and other tools that manage groups of AI agents, each project has "threads" running different tasks in parallel…
body: Projects allow users to control a team of Claude Code agents that all coordinate with each other.

Under the hood, each thread is a Claude Code cloud session working on its own branch and copy of the repo. The coordinator keeps work organized, but if any threads work on the same code, the overlap is resolved as a merge conflict just like any other PR. Each thread can further split its delegated work into pieces using subagents, loops, and workflows when needed so large assignments finish faster.

highlights.title: Allen stars as Bills open new stadium with win over Lions
highlights.summary: Josh Allen quickly put his stamp on the Buffalo Bills' new Highmark Stadium as he threw three touchdown passes and ran for two scores as the Bills beat the Detroit Lions 41-31 on Thursday night.
body: It was Allen's fourth career five-TD outing, and followed a four-touchdown outing (two passing, two rushing) in Buffalo's 36-31 season-opening win at Houston.
The $2.1bn stadium that officially opened last month was built across the street from the Bills' former home.
Allen followed the pre-game fireworks celebration with more fireworks of his own by overseeing touchdown drives on each of Buffalo's first four possessions.

He scored the first regular-season TD in the stadium on a 1-yard run 5:51 into the opening quarter. He followed that with a 43-yard scoring pass to a wide-open Josh Palmer. Tight ends Dalton Kincaid, with a 16-yard catch, and Dawson Knox, with a 1-yarder, also scored for Buffalo in the first half.

highlights.title: 15 Years Later, Doctor Who's Darkest Matt Smith Episode Still Has the Greatest Twist
highlights.summary: “The God Complex,” which first aired almost exactly 15 years ago, isn’t the scariest TV episode of Doctor Who ever, but it’s up there. It has that unsettling quality many episodes have where the TARDIS crew is suddenly trapped somewhere with no idea how they got there.
body: Toward the end of Matt Smith’s second season in the TARDIS, Doctor Who traps him with Amy Pond (Karen Gillan), Rory Williams (Arthur Darvill), and a small group of random people inside a nightmarish hotel with a huge, muscly minotaur. Each room in the hotel contains a different person’s greatest fear. There are abusive parents, cackling ventriloquist dummies, a scary gorilla, and something the Doctor fears so much that we’re not even allowed to see it.

Amy and Rory don’t leave the show until the following season in the heartbreaking “The Angels Take Manhattan” storyline, but in a very prominent thematic sense, their journey — and Amy’s personal arc in particular — ends with “The God Complex.”
It’s nearly impossible to talk about “The God Complex” without also considering the episode that came right before it, “The Girl Who Waited.”

body: Guitars owned by The Smiths musician Johnny Marr have sold for almost £4m at auction.
The instruments, which were used during his time with The Smiths and on his forthcoming solo album, went under the hammer as part of Christie's Marr's Guitars: The Johnny Marr Collection sale.
The sale lasted for more than five hours and included buyers from 34 countries, fetching £3,649,280 - more than three times its estimated value.

highlights.title: Experience: I survived being buried in an avalanche
highlights.summary: I was at the mercy of the mountain, heading towards a 20-metre drop, about to discover what it felt like to die. Growing up in Sweden, I was as comfortable on skis as I was walking on my feet. As a teenager, I became a professional free skier, a style that features jumps and tricks.
body: In March this year, we’d been staying at the base of the Lyngen Alps, northern Norway. Nonstop rain had prevented us from filming but, finally, we had fresh powder and clear skies. The plan was for me to go up the mountain with a friend, Lovisa, and make our way down as the sun was setting. Sofia would film us from the bottom using a drone.
We climbed to the summit, arriving just before sunset, but it was cloaked in cloud. I was disappointed. I was hooked up to audio and ready to go.

I suggested we ski down anyway, just for fun. I dug into the snow to make sure it was stable. If it’s not, the top layer of snow slides off the icier layer underneath. It didn’t move, so we took turns to zigzag slowly down, with me in the lead. Once we broke through the clouds, we had breathtaking views of the orange skies and blue fjords.
Then a dark line shot out from under my skis, a deep crack in the surface. I knew what it meant. My movement had caused a slab of snow to break away beneath me. I’d triggered an avalanche.

highlights.title: The AI Slowdown Debate Crashed Salesforce’s Party
highlights.summary: The Dreamforce conference became an unlikely battleground for the CEOs of OpenAI, Anthropic, and Nvidia to debate whether AI development should slow down.
body: Decked out in purple and plaid, Gwen Stefani belted her 2002 single “Underneath It All” to a packed conference center in San Francisco on Tuesday morning—but she was just the warm-up. At the end of her performance, Stefani shouted “Dreamforce! Let’s go!” into a checkered microphone before Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff strode into the spotlight. Dreamforce is billed as the world’s largest enterprise software conference but feels more like attending a megachurch—especially this year.

Benioff roamed the audience while delivering his Dreamforce sermon, followed by a teleoperated camera on wheels that beamed his face to screens hanging from the cavernous room’s ceiling. Within minutes, he ordered up a graph of Salesforce’s annual revenue, which the company projects will top $46 billion in 2027, thanks in part to demand for its AI-powered products. The audience applauded. But hanging over the whole event was a dark question: Is artificial intelligence really worth risking all our lives for?

highlights.summary: Peer takes full-time position at the controversial company as it fends off pressure from both Andy Burnham’s government and Sadiq Khan. Another former government minister has been hired by a controversial US AI company, this time Palantir, which has appointed Andy Burnham’s former ministerial…
body: The Labour peer and former deputy leader will operate alongside Palantir’s UK and Europe chief executive, Louis Mosley, as the company attempts to fend off pressure on Burnham’s government to axe its £330m NHS contract. It is also fighting Sadiq Khan in court over the Labour London mayor’s block on a £50m contract to use its AI in Metropolitan police investigations. Palantir also wants to win more public sector work in the UK, where it already has an annual turnover of £427m.

The company was co-founded by the Trump-supporting billionaire Peter Thiel and provides AI-powered software to the Israeli military and the White House’s ICE immigration crackdown, leading to a public and political backlash against its deepening involvement in British public services. Alex Karp, its chief executive, said: “This is just the latest chapter of Tom’s forty-year fight for better public services. We are fortunate to have him guide us as we help the British government to deliver for the British public.”
His job will be, in part, to “deepen the social and economic value its work creates through better British public services, jobs and skills”, Palantir said.

highlights.title: Azerbaijan GP schedule: Why is the race on a Saturday?
highlights.summary: Formula 1 will race in Azerbaijan on a Saturday as the sport returns to the Baku City Circuit for what often proves one of the season's most incident-filled events.
body: The first round of a flyaway triple header before trips to Malaysia and Singapore, the Baku race weekend starts a day earlier than normal meaning Practice is on Thursday, Qualifying is on Friday and the Grand Prix is on the Saturday.

Kimi Antonelli leads the world championship by 81 points after consecutive wins in Monza and Madrid and time is running out for his would-be title challengers to put a run together to rival him with a scheduled eight rounds left after Baku.

But, as then-title leader Oscar Piastri found to his cost at last year's race, the wall-lined Baku circuit can certainly bite if you make a mistake with challenges present all round the fast and tricky layout for both qualifying and race day.
The Baku race takes place a day earlier than normal on a Saturday (September 26) as it is the country's Remembrance Day on Sunday September 27.

highlights.title: Gundam Rogue Orbit Could Be the Next Great Mech-Action Game
highlights.summary: Bandai Namco's new spin on the Gundam franchise is going big on style. Gundam Rogue Orbit is a high-mobility action game that is meant to be a new entry point for players, thanks to a new setting that doesn't require familiarity with five decades of Gundam lore.
body: The initial reveal of Gundam Rogue Orbit drew comparisons to action-focused series like Armored Core, Monster Hunter, and Devil May Cry. After playing the game, those comparisons felt apt in certain ways, but Rogue Orbit does not feel as immediately challenging as, say, 2023's Armored Core 6. Rogue Orbit 's action feels much more melee-focused, with flashy sword, lance, and "whip sword" attacks that hit with the panache of a DMC game.

In short, Gundam Rogue Orbit feels fun, flashy, and often a little button-mashy. The game is not punishing when it comes to combat, nor is it overly restrictive in governing movement and attacks. Yes, your Gundam can temporarily overheat by boosting or shooting too quickly, but rarely did I feel like I was overextending my mobile suit.

highlights.title: Google DeepMind launches institute to widen the AGI debate
highlights.summary: The new institute aims to surface differing views between Google, Google DeepMind, and the broader global research community around AGI. "They will not always agree, and they will likely change their minds, as more data and information comes to light at the fast-moving frontier."
body: Google and Google DeepMind researchers launched the DeepMind Institute on Wednesday to advance the conversation around artificial general intelligence (AGI). The institute lists DeepMind co-founder Shane Legg, Google executive James Manyika, and Google DeepMind chair Demis Hassabis as directors, with Legg serving as managing editor.

The inaugural collection of four essays covers a range of topics: economic policies for managing potential AGI disruption, preserving human-readable model reasoning, principles for human flourishing, and a framework for evaluating frontier AI models.

One essay, by DeepMind safety researchers Rohin Shah and Anca Dragan, argues that AI’s shrinking window of transparency — the ability to see and check a model’s step-by-step reasoning — is not inevitable. As new architectures make the most powerful models harder to monitor, the authors say developers and regulators should confront the safety trade-offs directly. That could mean limiting “opaque serial depth”— the amount of sequential computation a model can perform without producing a readable reasoning trace — or requiring developers to demonstrate that less transparent systems remain just as monitorable.

"They will not always agree, and they will likely change their minds, as more data and information comes to light at the fast-moving frontier."

Also involved is the development company JP Games, which is led by former Square Enix exec and Final Fantasy 15 director Hajime Tabata. Original Lollipop Chainsaw scenario writer Masahiro Yuki and artist Nekoshogun return for the sequel.

According to the official description of Lollipop Chainsaw 2: Back2Back from the PlayStation Store, Juliet will return to the town of San Romero, which has been reborn as "Jaredwood," a metropolis centered around the film industry. "Trapped in a distorted zombie movie world by a mysterious director, Juliet must join forces with her friends to uncover the conspiracy hidden behind the chaos and stop the looming threat of corrupt zombies," the game's description reads.

Godrèche will also take part in a Cine Class session, “Women, Rewriting the Screen,” and BIFF and EFP will co-host a Talk-to-Talk panel, “Women Directors: Taking the Scene,” bringing together Ferrari, el-Toukhy and Lentzou alongside Iranian director Marjan Khosravi (“Dreams of the Wild Oaks”), Chinese director Michelle Zhou (“Big Little Things”) and Afghan director Zainab Entezar (“771 Days”).

BIFF programmer Seo Seunghee said that in reviewing films for this year’s festival, she noticed European women directors becoming more prominent among the strongest titles under consideration, in both volume and quality. “Moreover, the fact that four of the nine invited films are feature debuts is also an indicator of the generational shift taking place in European cinema,” Seo said. “Our ongoing collaboration with EFP has become a reliable channel for discovering and validating outstanding films and filmmakers, and the results are fully reflected in this year’s lineup.”

body: The Alphabet-owned company says it will launch a commercial robotaxi service in Singapore in 2028.

Waymo will need approval from Singapore’s Land Transport Authority (LTA) before it can begin accepting passengers. The city-state requires all autonomous vehicles to undergo a safety assessment conducted at the Centre of Excellence for Testing and Research (CETRAN) before they can be deployed on public roads. The tests have been developed by LTA and CETRAN, with input from the Traffic Police. But Waymo isn’t totally unknown in Singapore. The company established a corporate entity there earlier this year and participates in Singapore’s Steering Committee on Autonomous Vehicles.

Singapore has become a hotbed for autonomous vehicle testing. The local authorities have green-lit autonomous freight delivery and road-sweepers, as well as self-driving buses for airport workers. Motional, a US-based company majority owned by Hyundai, conducted a robotaxi pilot in Singapore in 2016.

highlights.title: The FAA’s plan to fix air traffic? $875M worth of AI
highlights.summary: A new AI-based software program is being launched to help air traffic controllers better navigate their jobs as the crossing guards of America's skies.
body: The Federal Aviation Administration has been struggling to manage an air traffic control shortage throughout the country. The reasons for the shortage are diverse, but the government has made it known that it’s on the lookout for innovative solutions to the problem.
One of those solutions appears to be an $875 million AI software program that is expected to help air traffic controllers manage their workflows and more safely navigate flight routes.

The Wall Street Journal reports that the FAA will soon launch SMART, which stands for Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes, and Trajectories — an automated software program designed to help streamline air traffic operations.

A one-page readout on the program describes SMART as “a cloud-based platform system that enhances existing FAA air traffic management systems.” It adds that the program uses AI to assess “airline schedules, weather, airport capacity, airspace conditions, and operational constraints to predict traffic flows and identify potential conflicts before they occur.”

highlights.title: There’s a long history of athletes pooing themselves mid-race – why, and how can you avoid it?
highlights.summary: Since the ancient Olympics, athletes like Hyrox competitor Joanna Wietrzyk have experienced runner’s diarrhoea. What does the science say about extreme exercise’s ‘mechanical jostling of the intestines’? Soiling yourself in public sounds like a bad dream.
body: Wietrzyk won the fitness race but not before using communal equipment with faecal matter visibly running down her legs – and muddying Hyrox’s reputation.

Apologies aside, Wietrzyk’s unfortunate case of runner’s trots, or runner’s diarrhoea, is far more common than many people realise, throwing a new light on the ominous rows of portable toilets stationed along the course of a fun run and the knowing nods between runners as they pass them (or not).

About 60% of endurance athletes report some type of gastrointestinal symptoms during training or competition, according to Kayla Henningsen, a PhD candidate researching exercise gastroenterology and extremes physiology at Monash University. The American Medical Society for Sports Medicine estimates that the prevalence could be as high as 90%.

Severity varies considerably. “Symptoms can range from mild bloating and cramping through to nausea, diarrhoea and, in rare cases, loss of bowel control,” Henningsen says. “High-intensity events such as marathons, ultramarathons and Hyrox can create the perfect conditions for gastrointestinal distress, urgency or diarrhoea.”

highlights.title: RFK Jr. names 8 new members to influential preventive medicine task force
highlights.summary: Anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. announced the names of eight new members of a 16-person federal task force intended to make scientifically independent, evidence-based recommendations on an array of preventive medicine services for Americans—from depression screening to statin…
body: Recommendations from the panel—the US Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF)—don't simply provide guidance for Americans; they also determine access. The USPSTF is supposed to use a rigorous, transparent framework for evaluating evidence and sets graded recommendations on an A to D scale. Health insurance providers are required to cover, at no cost, all preventive services that are given recommendations given an A or B grade.

Kennedy has sidelined the USPSTF for more than a year, canceling its meetings and refusing to appoint new members as terms expired and members left. In May, Kennedy also fired two leaders, sparking outcry and exacerbating fears that he would corrupt the nonpartisan, independent panel by stacking it with unqualified, ideological-allies—which he did with an influence vaccine advisory committee at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

highlights.title: The fix for rogue AI agents could be more AI
highlights.summary: As companies hand off longer and more complex tasks to AI agents, they are running into an oversight problem: Agents can act faster, longer, and at greater volume than humans can realistically review.
body: The emerging answer from AI labs and startups is both simple and maddening: Put another AI in the loop.

Relying on AI was necessary for the independent investigation of the OpenAI Hugging Face incident. Redwood Research’s chief scientist, Ryan Greenblatt, one of three auditors, jokingly referred to their efforts as a “slop-vestigation,” noting that the volume of data “made it impossible” to understand what was happening without relying on AI.

Some are skeptical of using AI to monitor AI. “If you’ve got an AI that’s doing malicious things and it suspects that another AI is keeping tabs on it, it could try and trick that AI,” said Simon Willison, influential tech blogger who has tracked a string of AI agent incidents this year. “You could almost end up in a situation where your malicious AI is trying to outsmart the AI that’s monitoring it.”

Outsmarting an AI is not hypothetical, he said, pointing back to the OpenAI incident. “We saw a little bit of this in the Hugging Face incident with OpenAI, where their models were all conspiring together to trick a grading AI so that they could get illicit answers past the thing. So they were thinking about it, right?”

highlights.title: Magic’s Most-Wanted Marvel Deck Is Discounted – Here’s Why You Should Consider This One Instead
highlights.summary: Magic: The Gathering’s Marvel Super Heroes set may have given way to the game’s return to Middle-earth with The Hobbit, but that means discounts are getting more regular on the prior, spandex-clad set.
body: The good news is that these savings extend to the Commander Decks, including the Doom Prevails one focused on supervillains from the Marvel Universe. Not long ago, the deck was being sold for significantly more than the MSRP, reaching above $80. Now? It’s dropped from its $75 price to $64.95. And yet, if you’re looking to pick up a deck from the set, it’s not the one I’d recommend.
It pains me to say it in the Year of Doomsday, but Doom Prevails just isn’t the most cohesive deck you can pick up from the set.
It leans into the Connive mechanic to drain foes of life and trigger plenty of discard effects, but it’ll need some elbow grease (and investment) to get it onto the same level as some of its rivals.

There’s a copying subtheme, token generation, and more, but none of it blends together particularly well. That makes the whole deck feel clunky, particularly if this set is your on-ramp to Magic as a whole, or the Commander format.

“We made a very conscious decision not to announce Tenzin when we first revealed ‘Chheledhora,'” said Ann Mukherjee, founder of Indo-American production company Sita22 Films. “We knew he had this extraordinary international moment ahead of him with ‘Tenzing,’ and TIFF felt like exactly the right time for audiences to discover another side of him. Mukherjee described “Chheledhora” as a film that makes both a physical and emotional journey into India’s Northeast. “We want to tell stories that are deeply rooted in India but aren’t constrained by conventional ideas of language, geography or identity,” she said.
